caveats.exception: The business word 'exception' means status PENDING_EXCEPTION: value that is pending approval and has not become a firm slip.
caveats.generated: GENERATED = ACTIVE, PAID, PAID_MANUAL, BROKEN, AUTO_BROKEN. It includes agreements that broke later: breaking is a later outcome and does not erase the generation. A broken slip stays in the issued denominator and never in the paid numerator.
caveats.first_installment: installment_no = 0 is the first installment. Never normalise it to 1.
caveats.portfolio: The portfolio name comes from debt_attributes.portfolio_label, not from a portfolio table.
caveats.agent_id: agent_id is the agent's public key (agents.login). agent_name is the display name.
caveats.cross_line: The same agent in two product lines is two separate entities per call. Rollups for 'all' lines sum counters first and recompute ratios once.
caveats.grain: Two grains of 'agreement count': agreement_count (per agreement) is used for rankings, ticket and conversion; agreement_count_by_contract (per contract) is for totals only.
caveats.answer_vs_cpc: Three different things: CPC is a count; answer rate = answer_count / attempt_count; CPC rate = cpc_count / answer_count. Do not confuse a column name with a definition.
caveats.denominator: Every risk percentage uses the same denominator: the first-installment universe of the window = generated (ACTIVE, PAID, PAID_MANUAL, BROKEN, AUTO_BROKEN) + exception + rejected value. Each axis is a slice between 0 and 100% of that universe.
caveats.thresholds: Risk level from composite risk: low <= 20.0%, medium <= 40.0%, high above. These cut-offs are configuration, not universal truths. Any axis outside 0..100% is a data anomaly and must be flagged.
caveats.anomaly: An axis outside 0..100% cannot happen with clean data: every axis is a slice of a universe that contains it. Report it as suspected corruption (negative amounts, mismatched windows), never as real risk and never corrected.
caveats.slip_maturity: A slip counts as unpaid until it is paid. With a grace period of 3 days, slips issued in the last days look worse than they will.
caveats.excluded_agents: Agents whose login matches an excluded pattern are removed in SQL, never afterwards: system%, test%.

attempt_count.formula: number of outreach events in the window

answer_count.formula: outreach events whose result is flagged answered

cpc.formula: cpc_count = outreach events flagged answered AND right_party. A count, never a percentage.

answer_rate_pct.formula: answer_count / attempt_count * 100. Always label it 'answer rate', never 'CPC'.

conversion_pct.formula: agreement_count / cpc_count * 100: generated agreements over right-party contacts. The denominator is CPC, not slips issued.
conversion_pct.note: Only exists at agent grain: there is no daily, portfolio or product-line series.

paid_per_cpc_pct.formula: slips_paid / cpc_count * 100. A different metric: never call it conversion.

slip_effectiveness_pct.formula: slips paid within the grace period / slips issued * 100, by issue date
slip_effectiveness_pct.note: Not conversion. Recent days are immature because their grace period may still be running.

first_installment_value.formula: SUM(amount) of installment 0 of generated agreements issued in the window

agreement_value.formula: SUM(amount) over all installments of generated agreements whose first installment was issued in the window

agreement_count.formula: COUNT(DISTINCT agreement_id) with a generated first installment in the window (agreement grain)

agreement_count_by_contract.formula: COUNT(DISTINCT agreement_id, portfolio_id, debt_id) through agreement_debts (contract grain)
agreement_count_by_contract.note: Never use it as a denominator. Ticket and conversion use the agreement grain.

generated_value.formula: first_installment_value over generated statuses, per day

daily_pace.formula: Always TODAY according to the agent clock, whatever the session window is. Baseline estimator: mean hourly profile of recent history.

composite_risk_formula.formula: MAX(exception_pct, broken_pct, rejected_pct). Never the sum: the axes overlap (broken is a subset of generated), so adding them double counts and overstates risk. A portfolio's risk is its worst axis.
